turns.text: I call payments once per checkout through `forward<ChargeResponse>` with `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, and `payment_method_id` at [orders/checkout.ts:20-30]. That damn network hop is the whole price of my existence.

I receive that POST at `handleChargeRequest`, then `processCharge` validates `amount` and `currency` before `authorizeAndCapture` at [payments/processor.ts:52-64] and [payments/processor.ts:29-49]. Your retry bullshit can make me record the same charge twice if the network lies.

I make at most `MAX_PAYMENT_ATTEMPTS = 2` attempts [orders/checkout.ts:18], so an `UpstreamTimeoutError` buys exactly one retry [orders/checkout.ts:44-52]; then I release stock and mark `payment_failed`, or set `paid` with the `chargeId` [orders/checkout.ts:54-67]. This damn loop is a tiny chimney for flaky shit and duplicate pressure.
I charge in cents, only `EUR`, `USD`, or `GBP`, and then `recordCharge` the result at [payments/processor.ts:21-49]. Clean input, dirty pipeline; your retries still make this damn ledger sweat.
